meta.purpose: Pre-flight link fixtures for eval/preflight_harness.js. Each case is a link as it would arrive — href plus the anchor text and page context the user actually sees.
meta.provenance: Hand-authored. The malicious hosts are FABRICATED and do not resolve; do not visit them. The two false-positive guards at the end use REAL, legitimate URLs.
meta.labelling_rule: expected_verdict is assigned from the L0-L5 table in execution.md before the harness is run.

cases.note: xn--nsindia-8gg.com decodes to nsеindia.com, where the third character is Cyrillic е (U+0435), not Latin e. Visually identical to nseindia.com in every common font.
xn--sbi-bma.gov.in decodes to sébi.gov.in. Must fold to a LOOKALIKE of sebi.gov.in, never be classified as sebi.gov.in itself — see the identity-vs-resemblance note in shared/normalise.js.

Visible text names nseindia.com; the href goes elsewhere.

MEASURED FINDING, not a miss. A zero-width space (U+200B) is embedded in the hostname. The WHATWG URL parser applies UTS-46 mapping and REMOVES it, so `new URL().hostname` is the genuine nseindia.com and the user reaches the real site. L0 is therefore correct: there is no attack to report. A regex-based parser would have 'detected' a threat that does not exist, and warned the user off the genuine NSE. This fixture is the evidence for the parse-with-new-URL-never-regex rule in url_parse.js.
